L24: # FwpmFilterAdd0 function (fwpmu.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The FwpmFilterAdd0 function adds a new filter object to the system.
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `DWORD FwpmFilterAdd0(
L37:       [in]            HANDLE               engineHandle,
L38:       [in]            const FWPM_FILTER0   *filter,
L39:       [in, optional]  PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR sd,
L40:       [out, optional] UINT64               *id
L41:     );
L42:     `
L43: ## Parameters
L44: 
L45: `[in] engineHandle`
L46: 
L47: Type: HANDLE
L48: 
L49: Handle for an open session to the filter engine. Call cite5†FwpmEngineOpen0 to open a session to the filter engine.
L50: 
L51: `[in] filter`
L52: 
L53: Type: cite6†FWPM_FILTER0 *
L54: 
L55: The filter object to be added.
L56: 
L57: `[in, optional] sd`
L58: 
L59: Type: cite7†SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR L60: 
L61: Security information about the filter object.
L62: 
L63: `[out, optional] id`
L64: 
L65: Type: UINT64*
L66: 
L67: The runtime identifier for this filter.
L68: ## Return value
L69: 
L70: Type: DWORD
L71: Return code/value  | Description
L72: --- | ---
L73: ERROR_SUCCESS
L74: 0  | The filter was successfully added.
L75: ERROR_INVALID_SECURITY_DESCR
L76: 0x8007053A  | The security descriptor structure is invalid. Or, a filter condition contains a security descriptor in absolute format.
L77: FWP_E_CALLOUT_NOTIFICATION_FAILED
L78: 0x80320037  | The caller added a callout filter and the callout returned an error from its notification routine.
L79: FWP_E_* error code
L80: 0x80320001—0x80320039  | A Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) specific error. See cite8†WFP Error Codes for details.
L81: RPC_* error code
L82: 0x80010001—0x80010122  | Failure to communicate with the remote or local firewall engine.
L83: ## Remarks
L84: 
L85: FwpmFilterAdd0 adds the filter to the specified sub-layer at every filtering layer in the system.
L86: 
L87: Some fields in the cite6†FWPM_FILTER0 structure are assigned by the system, not the caller, and are ignored in the call to FwpmFilterAdd0.
L88: 
L89: If the caller supplies a NULL security descriptor, the system will assign a default security descriptor.
L90: To block connections to particular locations, add a cite9†FWP_ACTION_BLOCK filter specifying the local address at the cite10†FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V* layer, or add a FWP_ACTION_BLOCK filter without specifying the local address at the FWPM_LAYER_ALE_RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_V* layer.
L91: 
L92: Note
L93: 
L94: If a local address is specified at the resource assignment layer, an implicit bind would succeed because address, address type, and port may come back as cite11†FWP_EMPTY .
L95: The cite6†FWPM_FILTER0 structure can label a filter as a boot-time or persistent filter. Boot-time filters are added to the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) when the TCP/IP driver starts, and are removed once the BFE finishes initialization. Persistent objects are added when the BFE starts.
L96: 
L97: This function cannot be called from within a read-only transaction. It will fail with FWP_E_INCOMPATIBLE_TXN. See cite12†Object Management for more information about transactions.
L98: 
L99: The caller needs the following access rights:
L100:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD access to the filter's container
L101:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK access to the provider (if any)
L102:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK access to the applicable layer
L103:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK access to the applicable sub-layer
L104:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK access to the callout (if any)
L105:   * cite13†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK access to the provider context (if any).
L106: 
L107: See cite14†Access Control for more information.
L108: 
L109: To add a filter that references a callout, invoke the functions in the following order.
L110:   * Call cite15†FwpsCalloutRegister0 (documented in the Windows Driver Kit (WDK)), to register the callout with the filter engine.
L111:   * Call cite16†FwpmCalloutAdd0 to add the callout to the system.
L112:   * Call FwpmFilterAdd0 to add the filter that references the callout to the system.
L113: 
L114: By default filters that reference callouts that have been added but have not yet registered with the filter engine are treated as Block filters.
L115: FwpmFilterAdd0 is a specific implementation of FwpmFilterAdd. See cite17†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows for more information.
L116: #### Examples
L117: The following C++ example shows how to initialize and add a filter using FwpmFilterAdd0 that
L118: specifically blocks traffic on IP V4 for all applications.
L119: 
L120:     `
L121:     // Add filter to block traffic on IP V4 for all applications.
L122:     //
L123:     FWPM_FILTER0      fwpFilter;
L124:     FWPM_SUBLAYER0    fwpFilterSubLayer;
L125: 
L126:     RtlZeroMemory(&fwpFilter, sizeof(FWPM_FILTER0));
L127: 
L128:     fwpFilter.layerKey = FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4;
L129:     fwpFilter.action.type = FWP_ACTION_BLOCK;
L130:     if (&fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey != NULL)
L131:         fwpFilter.subLayerKey = fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey;
L132: 
L133:     fwpFilter.weight.type = FWP_EMPTY; // auto-weight.
L134:     fwpFilter.numFilterConditions = 0; // this applies to all application traffic
L135:     fwpFilter.displayData.name = L"Receive/Accept Layer Block";
L136:     fwpFilter.displayData.description = L"Filter to block all inbound connections.";
L137: 
L138:     printf("Adding filter to block all inbound connections.\n");
L139:     result = FwpmFilterAdd0(engineHandle, &fwpFilter, NULL, NULL);
L140: 
L141:     if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)
L142:         printf("FwpmFilterAdd0 failed. Return value: %d.\n", result);
L143:     else
L144:         printf("Filter added successfully.\n");
L145: 
L146:     `

L24: # FWPM_SESSION0 structure (fwpmtypes.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The FWPM_SESSION0 structure stores the state associated with a client session.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `typedef struct FWPM_SESSION0_ {
L36:       GUID               sessionKey;
L37:       FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 displayData;
L38:       UINT32             flags;
L39:       UINT32             txnWaitTimeoutInMSec;
L40:       DWORD              processId;
L41:       SID                *sid;
L42:       wchar_t            *username;
L43:       BOOL               kernelMode;
L44:     } FWPM_SESSION0;
L45:     `
L46: ## Members
L47: 
L48: `sessionKey`
L49: 
L50: Uniquely identifies the session.
L51: 
L52: If this member is zero in the call to cite5†FwpmEngineOpen0 , Base Filtering Engine (BFE) will generate a GUID.
L53: 
L54: `displayData`
L55: 
L56: Allows sessions to be annotated in a human-readable form.
L57: 
L58: See cite6†FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 for more information.
L59: 
L60: `flags`
L61: 
L62: Settings to control session behavior.
L63: 
L64: Session flag  | Meaning
L65: --- | ---
L66: FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC
L67:  | When this flag is set, any objects added during the session are automatically deleted when the session ends.
L68: 
L69: FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_RESERVED
L70:  | Reserved.
L71: 
L72: `txnWaitTimeoutInMSec`
L73: 
L74: Time in milli-seconds that a client will wait to begin a transaction.
L75: 
L76: If this member is zero, BFE will use a default timeout.
L77: 
L78: `processId`
L79: 
L80: Process ID of the client.
L81: 
L82: `sid`
L83: 
L84: SID of the client.
L85: 
L86: `username`
L87: 
L88: User name of the client.
L89: 
L90: `kernelMode`
L91: 
L92: TRUE if this is a kernel-mode client.
L93: ## Remarks
L94: 
L95: This structure contains information supplied by the client when creating a session by calling cite5†FwpmEngineOpen0 , or information retrieved from the system when enumerating sessions by calling cite7†FwpmSessionEnum0 .
L96: 
L97: The members processId, sid, username, and kernelMode are not supplied by the client. They are supplied by BFE and can be retrieved when enumerating sessions.
L98: FWPM_SESSION0 is a specific implementation of FWPM_SESSION. See cite8†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows for more information.

L24: # Access control (Windows Filtering Platform)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: In Windows Filtering Platform (WFP), the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) service implements the standard cite5†Windows access control model based on access tokens and security descriptors.
L33: ## Access control model
L34: 
L35: Security descriptors can be specified when adding new WFP objects, such as filters and sub-layers. Security descriptors are managed using the WFP management functions Fwpm*GetSecurityInfo0 and Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0, where * stands for the WFP object's name. These functions are semantically identical to the Windows cite6†GetSecurityInfo and cite7†SetSecurityInfo functions.
L36: 
L37: Note
L38: 
L39: The Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions cannot be called from within an explicit transaction.
L40: 
L41: Note
L42: The Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions can only be called from within a dynamic session if they are being used to manage a dynamic object created within the same session.
L43: 
L44: The default security descriptor for the filter engine (the root Engine object in the diagram below) is as follows.
L45:   * Grant GENERIC_ALL (GA) access rights to the built-in Administrators group.
L46:   * Grant GENERIC_READ (GR) GENERIC_WRITE (GW) GENERIC_EXECUTE (GX) access rights to network configuration operators.
L47:   * Grant GRGWGX access rights to the following service security identifiers (SSIDs): MpsSvc (Windows Firewall), NapAgent (Network Access Protection Agent), PolicyAgent (IPsec Policy Agent), RpcSs (Remote Procedure Call), and WdiServiceHost (Diagnostic Service Host).
L48:   * Grant FWPM_ACTRL_OPEN and FWPM_ACTRL_CLASSIFY to everyone. (These are WFP-specific access rights, described in table below.)
L49: The remaining default security descriptors are derived through inheritance.
L50: There are some access checks, such as for Fwpm*Add0, Fwpm*CreateEnumHandle0, Fwpm*SubscribeChanges0 function calls, that cannot be done at the individual object level. For these functions, there are container objects for each object type. For the standard object types (for example, providers, callouts, filters), the existing Fwpm*GetSecurityInfo0 and Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions are overloaded, such that a null GUID parameter identifies the associated container.
L51: For the other object types (for example, network events and IPsec security associations), there are explicit functions for managing the container's security information.
L52: BFE supports automatic inheritance of Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) access control entries (ACEs). BFE does not support System Access Control List (SACL) ACEs. Objects inherit ACEs from their container. Containers inherit ACEs from the filter engine. The propagation paths are shown in the diagram below.
L53: 
L54: cite8†Image: Diagram that shows the ACE propagation paths, starting with 'Engine'. L55: For the standard object types, BFE enforces all the generic and standard access rights. In addition, WFP defines the following specific access rights.
L56: WFP Access right  | Description
L57: --- | ---
L58: FWPM_ACTRL_ADD
L59:  | Required to add an object to a container.
L60: FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK
L61:  | Required to create an association to an object. For example, to add a filter that references a callout, the caller must have ADD_LINK access to the callout.
L62: FWPM_ACTRL_BEGIN_READ_TXN
L63:  | Required to begin an explicit read transaction.
L64: FWPM_ACTRL_BEGIN_WRITE_TXN
L65:  | Required to begin an explicit write transaction.
L66: FWPM_ACTRL_CLASSIFY
L67:  | Required to classify against a user-mode layer.
L68: FWPM_ACTRL_ENUM
L69:  | Required to enumerate the objects in a container. However, the enumerator only returns objects to which the caller has FWPM_ACTRL_READ access.
L70: FWPM_ACTRL_OPEN
L71:  | Required to open a session with BFE.
L72: FWPM_ACTRL_READ
L73:  | Required to read an object's properties.
L74: FWPM_ACTRL_READ_STATS
L75:  | Required to read statistics.
L76: FWPM_ACTRL_SUBSCRIBE
L77:  | Required to subscribe for notifications. Subscribers will only receive notifications for objects to which they have FWPM_ACTRL_READ access.
L78: FWPM_ACTRL_WRITE
L79:  | Required to set engine options.
L80: BFE skips all access checks for kernel-mode callers.

This document is intended to help network admins, support engineers, and developers to investigate UWP app network connectivity issues.

This document guides you through steps to debug Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app network connectivity issues by providing practical examples.

## Typical causes of connectivity issues

UWP app network connectivity issues are typically caused by:

  1. The UWP applications not being permitted to receive loopback traffic. This permission must be configured. By default, UWP applications aren't allowed to receive loopback traffic
  2. The UWP app is missing the proper capability tokens
  3. The private range is configured incorrectly. For example, the private range is set incorrectly through GP/MDM policies, etc.

To understand these causes more thoroughly, there are several concepts to review.

This document is intended to help network admins, support engineers, and developers to investigate UWP app network connectivity issues.

This document guides you through steps to debug Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app network connectivity issues by providing practical examples.

## Typical causes of connectivity issues

UWP app network connectivity issues are typically caused by:

  1. The UWP applications not being permitted to receive loopback traffic. This permission must be configured. By default, UWP applications aren't allowed to receive loopback traffic
  2. The UWP app is missing the proper capability tokens
  3. The private range is configured incorrectly. For example, the private range is set incorrectly through GP/MDM policies, etc.

To understand these causes more thoroughly, there are several concepts to review.

The traffic of network packets (what's permitted and what's not) on Windows is determined by the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). When a UWP app or the private range is configured incorrectly, it affects how the UWP app's network traffic will be processed by WFP.

When a packet is processed by WFP, the characteristics of that packet must explicitly match all the conditions of a filter to either be permitted or dropped to its target address. Connectivity issues typically happen when the packet doesn't match any of the filter conditions, leading the packet to be dropped by a default block filter. The presence of the default block filters ensures network isolation for UWP applications. Specifically, it guarantees a network drop for a packet that doesn't have the correct capabilities for the resource it's trying to reach. Such a packet drop ensures the application's granular access to each resource type and preventing the application from escaping its environment.

For more information on the filter arbitration algorithm and network isolation, see Filter Arbitration and Isolation.

The following sections cover debugging case examples for loopback and non-loopback UWP app network connectivity issues.

## Debugging UWP App Loopback scenarios

If you need to establish a TCP/IP connection between two processes on the same host where one of them is a UWP app, you must enable loopback.

To enable loopback for client outbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:

Windows Command Prompt

Copy
    
    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -a -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>
    `

To enable loopback for server inbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:

Windows Command Prompt

Copy
    
    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -is -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>
    `

You can ensure loopback is enabled by checking the appx manifests of both the sender and receiver.

For more information about loopback scenarios, see Communicating with localhost (loopback).

Note

If you are in the middle of developing a UWA application and want to test its loopback, ensure to uninstall and re-install the UWA app if the network capabilities change for whatever reason.

Also, see How to enable loopback and troubleshoot network isolation (Windows Runtime apps).

If you can consistently reproduce the issue, then you can run the following command in an admin command prompt to gather a fresh trace:

    <Run UWP app>
    Netsh wfp capture stop
    `

These commands generate a wfpdiag.cab. Inside the .cab exists a wfpdiag.xml, which contains any allow or drop netEvents and filters that existed during that repro. Without "keywords=19", the trace will only collect drop netEvents.

Inside the wfpdiag.xml, search for netEvents that have FWPM_NET_EVENT_TYPE_CLASSIFY_DROP as the netEvent type. To find the relevant drop events, search for the drop events with matching destination IP address, package SID, or application ID name. During quarantine, all new inbound connections without exceptions are blocked.

This document describes the quarantine feature and explains why the application traffic could be blocked by quarantine.

## Quarantine filters

The quarantine feature creates filters that can be split into three categories:

  * Quarantine default inbound block filter
  * Quarantine default exception filters
  * Interface unquarantine filters

These filters are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_QUARANTINE` sublayer and these layers are:

  1. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4`
  2. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V6`
  3. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4`
  4. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V6`

Note

Any firewall rules added by policy settings don't affect the filters in the quarantine sublayer. Filters from firewall rules are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_WF` sublayer. In other words, you can't add your own exception filters to prevent packets from being evaluated by quarantine filters.

For more information about WFP layers and sublayers, see WFP Operation.

### Quarantine default inbound block filter

The quarantine default inbound block filter blocks any new nonloopback inbound connections, unless the packet isn't explicitly permitted by another filter in the quarantine sublayer.

### Quarantine default exception filters

When the interface is in quarantine state, the quarantine default exception filters permit new inbound connections given that they meet the conditions of an exception filter. One example of the exception filters is the quarantine default inbound loopback exception filter. This exception filter allows all loopback packets when the interface is in quarantine state.

### Interface unquarantine filter

The interface unquarantine filters allow all nonloopback packets if the interface is successfully categorized.

*** Add File: D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/workflow/design/after-wifi-negative-04.md
+# vg-spec1 关闭Wi-Fi负控后的备选判定 v4.0
+
+- 方案角色会话：`01a148da-3f4c-7540-90e9-22b4485815b4`。
+- 本轮只读本题证据、现有通用CLI帮助及微软/华为官方文档；仅新增本文。未下载/安装工具、未启动实例、未改网络/防火墙/权限、未改生产测试状态。
+
+## 1. 当前结论
+
+用户本轮关闭Wi-Fi的方法已被同NAT负控否定：仍有HEAD×2、GET200/1324字节并到达原第二层预览，eth0 UP、IsAvailable=1、LinkUp=1。它不是本题真实离线；runner保留FAIL等待用户恢复Wi-Fi是正确处理，不应把ACK或界面图标替代网络证据。
+
+**现有6.1/6.1.1工具没有已确认可立即执行的官方断网入口。普通Windows按程序防火墙规则也不能在当前证据下保证切断本题loopback NAT。**有一个新的、有微软官方API依据的备选：管理员运行一个本题专用的用户态WFP动态过滤辅助工具，在ALE连接授权层按Emulator程序身份直接阻断出站连接。该方案可覆盖loopback，原则上可保留HDC入站控制，但它需要额外工具实现、人工管理员授权和设施验证；不能宣称已可执行或已获得guest系统LinkDown。
+
+若不引入这个管理员WFP工具，且继续要求真实guest断网，最窄外部条件是提供官方支持该能力的Emulator26.0.0工具及经实测可切断虚拟Ethernet/NAT的镜像组合。用户当前明确不下载新工具，因此本轮不执行下载，也不能消除该外部条件后虚报通过。
+
+## 2. 本题路径与新只读证据
+
+| 项 | 证据 | 判断 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 用户关闭Wi-Fi后的负控 | 根Agent派工已给HEAD×2/GET2001324、预览及系统状态；原始目录 `logs/development-round-02/manual-offline-round-01/test_13_actual_offline_three_cancels_and_restore/`，含 `user-disconnected-network-state.json` 与 `offline-connection-negative-control/`。 | NAT仍通，G2离线前置失败；不能继续把离线三取消算pass。 |
+| host服务实际监听 | `hypium_tests/evidence.py:257` 为 `ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler)`，不是host外部网卡地址。 | guest10.0.2.2服务最终是host loopback；只断公网、DNS或某物理网卡不等于切该路径。 |
+| 当前Emulator | 只读CIM见PID27612，路径 `D:/HarmonyDev/DevEcoStudio-6.1.0/tools/emulator/Emulator.exe`，实例VgSpec1ManualOffline，HDC11237；同进程监听/已建立HDC均host127.0.0.1，另有外联49.4.40.74:5223。 | 不能笼统封全部loopback来假定保留HDC；需要区分出站NAT与入站控制。 |
+| 本机新旧工具版本 | `.../DevEcoStudio-6.1.0/tools/emulator/sdk-pkg.json` 为6.1.0.500；`.../DevEcoStudio/tools/emulator/sdk-pkg.json` 为6.1.1.360。 | 6.1.1不等于26。 |
+| 6.1.1基础CLI帮助 | 本轮Python capture `.../DevEcoStudio/tools/emulator/Emulator.exe -help` exit0；新增scenario为旋转、折叠、音量、电池、GPS、传感器等；未列network/link/disconnect/drop/packetloss开关。 | 不能将切换到已安装6.1.1当作已确认断网方案；不猜隐藏参数或私有接口。 |
+| 防火墙按程序参数 | 本轮 `Get-Command New-NetFirewallRule` 只读参数清单有Program、地址/端口、用户/服务等，没有ProcessId。 | 程序规则绑定可执行路径，不能称精确PID隔离；同路径其他实例也会受影响。 |
+| 当前权限 | 本轮 `ctypes.windll.shell32.IsUserAnAdmin()` 返回0；此前token为Medium/Administrators deny-only。 | 无可直接增加主机网络过滤策略的提升权限。 |
+
+6.1.1的CLI帮助不能证明所有UI绝无任何隐藏功能；本结论是**未发现受支持可执行入口**，因此不让用户盲试同类图标。此前旧工具飞行模式、smode拒绝、代理失败已充分记录，本轮不重试。
+
+## 3. localhost是否被防火墙排除：必须区分两个层面
+
+### 3.1 普通Windows Firewall程序规则
+
+[微软程序规则指南](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-firewall/best-practices-configuring)支持按程序路径及端口等条件阻断出站；[New-NetFirewallRule参考](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netsecurity/new-netfirewallrule)同样提供Program条件。但这两份文档不能证明本机Win32 loopback连接一定会被该规则拦住，也未提供本题精确PID过滤承诺。
+
+本轮没有在官方一手文档中取得“普通程序规则在当前Windows构建必定过滤/必定全豁免所有loopback”的完整契约，因此不能选择其中任一极端作为已证事实。微软另有AppContainer loopback隔离文档，其对象是UWP/AppContainer，不可直接套用到本题未打包的Win32 Emulator.exe；也不能用CheckNetIsolation开关替代普通进程隔离。
+
+结论：可以把普通程序规则作为需要管理员的**设施实验**，但没有足够证据承诺它能切10.0.2.2→127.0.0.1 NAT；添加规则成功或公网失败均不构成通过。当前任务已有明确loopback负控要求，不建议先增加一套不确定规则再请求用户盲试。
+
+### 3.2 Windows Filtering Platform本身可以过滤loopback
+
+[微软Filtering condition flags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/filtering-condition-flags-)明确提供 `FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK`，适用于ALE_AUTH_CONNECT及ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT等层。因此“所有Windows过滤层都不可能阻断localhost”是不成立的。
+
+[ALE说明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/application-layer-enforcement--ale-)支持按规范化程序文件名识别应用；[ALE层说明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/ale-layers)说明AUTH_CONNECT对应TCP connect及首个UDP/ICMP出站；[FwpmFilterAdd0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0)支持加入BLOCK过滤器。
+
+这证明存在可设计的官方API路径；它不是New-NetFirewallRule已经承诺的行为，也不是本轮已实现的工具。
+
+## 4. 条件化备选A：用户态WFP动态过滤工具
+
+此节只给root可评估的最小范围，不实施、不要求安装内核驱动或第三方网络工具。[微软User Mode vs. Kernel Mode指南](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/callout-driver-programming-considerations)建议可用标准过滤完成的工作采用用户态管理程序，避免写callout驱动。
+
+### 最小技术方案
+
+1. 本题logs下独立辅助进程使用系统Fwpuclnt.dll；打开 `FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC` 会话，在事务内加入本题独立标记/子层及两个IPv4/IPv6 `FWP_ACTION_BLOCK` 过滤器。
+2. 层只选 `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4/V6`，条件为 `FWPM_CONDITION_ALE_APP_ID` 等于本题实际Emulator.exe规范化路径，**不排除loopback**，也不只屏蔽WebDAV某个端口。这样目标是阻断该模拟器所有出站NAT连接，而非制造单服务失败。
+3. 不在AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT/LISTEN/RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT层放Block，不更改全局默认策略，不阻断host其他程序。当前HDC是hdc客户端向Emulator11237监听口发起的入站连接，因此预期不命中该出站过滤。这是根据本机socket与ALE层行为作的推断，必须用HDC心跳和重连实测，不能承诺。
+4. Program身份仍是路径，不是PID。预检必须确认同路径只有本题实例，实验期间禁止启动同路径其他实例；如无法保证则不能称仅影响本题。不要伪称FWPM_SESSION0.processId字段是过滤目标PID——它是管理会话客户端信息。
+5. 通过动态会话生命周期恢复：显式close引擎/退出辅助进程即自动移除该会话对象；另保留可复核filter ID和按本题GUID删除的恢复操作。不得设置persistent/boot-time过滤，不禁用Windows Firewall/BFE或修改其ACL。
+6. 产品负控前先结束既有应用恢复任务，断开应用旧连接。ALE为有状态过滤，不能拿旧长连接的行为猜测新连接结果；新应用请求和WFP drop记录须对应时间窗与Emulator appId。
+
+[FWPM_SESSION0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_session0)明确动态会话结束自动删除对象。[Access Control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/access-control)说明BFE默认授管理员完整权限，普通Everyone只保证OPEN/CLASSIFY；增加过滤器还需ADD/ADD_LINK等权限。当前token不满足，必须由用户人工处理UAC/以管理员运行已审查的辅助工具，或现有合法委派；不能绕过提升、悄悄改ACL。
+
+### 成立闸门与限制
+
+- root须先实现并审查辅助工具及异常退出回滚；本轮没有现成已验真的命令行程序，不能用文档API当已建成的方案。
+- 按v3的同endpoint在线正控→辅助工具生效→相同应用继续负控失败/活服务零到达→退出辅助工具→相同HEAD/GET恢复正控执行；加host其他程序仍可访问服务、HDC持续心跳/重连及明确的WFP drop/filter ID证据。
+- 此方法实际阻断NAT出站流量，但不会自动把guest eth0设LinkDown或NetConn IsAvailable=0。若本轮要求是系统网络状态“没有默认网络”的完整离线，此方法**只能提供真实传输隔离**，不能直接替代guest系统断网；必须保留这个边界并交root按既有验收口径审查，不能悄悄降格。
+- 若任一NAT HEAD/GET仍到达、HDC失联或其他host程序受影响，马上退出动态会话恢复并记录设施实验失败，不能靠改endpoint/关服务补出零请求。
+
+故A是有官方技术依据但需要管理员与本题辅助程序开发的选项，非当前权限下可直接执行的推荐动作。
+
+## 5. 条件化备选B：官方Emulator26的最窄外部条件
+
+[华为官方网络教程](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-emulator-access-network#section115741355151910)明确旧模拟器虚拟Ethernet常连，断host网络或模拟器Wi-Fi不能完全断网；从26.0.0起才支持控制中心飞行模式断网仿真。[26发布说明](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-releases/deveco-studio-new-features-2600)给出工具版本26.0.0.400。该证据已在v2通过公开官方正文取得。
+
+若不接受A的管理员/辅助工具/仅传输隔离限制，完成本题真实guest offline至少需要：
+
+1. **官方来源、校验完备的Emulator26.0.0.400或后续明确支持断网仿真的工具**，并排目录；不用升级本题工程、旧SDK或现有实例。
+2. **被该工具实际支持且断网功能成立的guest镜像组合**。可以先新建本题API23实例验证；若旧guest不响应，则需新版官方镜像的新本题实例。不能仅凭host工具版本保证API23断网生效。
+3. **HDC能在官方断网模式中保持控制，并经同NAT正负正控证明**；新实例仍可用1308×2880/560dpi和同一冻结HAP/fixtures，不需要额外实体设备。

# vg-spec1 关闭Wi-Fi负控后的备选判定 v4.0

- 方案角色会话：`01a148da-3f4c-7540-90e9-22b4485815b4`。
- 本轮只读本题证据、现有通用CLI帮助及微软/华为官方文档；仅新增本文。未下载/安装工具、未启动实例、未改网络/防火墙/权限、未改生产测试状态。

## 1. 当前结论

用户本轮关闭Wi-Fi的方法已被同NAT负控否定：仍有HEAD×2、GET200/1324字节并到达原第二层预览，eth0 UP、IsAvailable=1、LinkUp=1。它不是本题真实离线；runner保留FAIL等待用户恢复Wi-Fi是正确处理，不应把ACK或界面图标替代网络证据。

**现有6.1/6.1.1工具没有已确认可立即执行的官方断网入口。普通Windows按程序防火墙规则也不能在当前证据下保证切断本题loopback NAT。**有一个新的、有微软官方API依据的备选：管理员运行一个本题专用的用户态WFP动态过滤辅助工具，在ALE连接授权层按Emulator程序身份直接阻断出站连接。该方案可覆盖loopback，原则上可保留HDC入站控制，但它需要额外工具实现、人工管理员授权和设施验证；不能宣称已可执行或已获得guest系统LinkDown。

若不引入这个管理员WFP工具，且继续要求真实guest断网，最窄外部条件是提供官方支持该能力的Emulator26.0.0工具及经实测可切断虚拟Ethernet/NAT的镜像组合。用户当前明确不下载新工具，因此本轮不执行下载，也不能消除该外部条件后虚报通过。

## 2. 本题路径与新只读证据

| 项 | 证据 | 判断 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 用户关闭Wi-Fi后的负控 | 根Agent派工已给HEAD×2/GET2001324、预览及系统状态；原始目录 `logs/development-round-02/manual-offline-round-01/test_13_actual_offline_three_cancels_and_restore/`，含 `user-disconnected-network-state.json` 与 `offline-connection-negative-control/`。 | NAT仍通，G2离线前置失败；不能继续把离线三取消算pass。 |
| host服务实际监听 | `hypium_tests/evidence.py:257` 为 `ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler)`，不是host外部网卡地址。 | guest10.0.2.2服务最终是host loopback；只断公网、DNS或某物理网卡不等于切该路径。 |
| 当前Emulator | 只读CIM见PID27612，路径 `D:/HarmonyDev/DevEcoStudio-6.1.0/tools/emulator/Emulator.exe`，实例VgSpec1ManualOffline，HDC11237；同进程监听/已建立HDC均host127.0.0.1，另有外联49.4.40.74:5223。 | 不能笼统封全部loopback来假定保留HDC；需要区分出站NAT与入站控制。 |
| 本机新旧工具版本 | `.../DevEcoStudio-6.1.0/tools/emulator/sdk-pkg.json` 为6.1.0.500；`.../DevEcoStudio/tools/emulator/sdk-pkg.json` 为6.1.1.360。 | 6.1.1不等于26。 |
| 6.1.1基础CLI帮助 | 本轮Python capture `.../DevEcoStudio/tools/emulator/Emulator.exe -help` exit0；新增scenario为旋转、折叠、音量、电池、GPS、传感器等；未列network/link/disconnect/drop/packetloss开关。 | 不能将切换到已安装6.1.1当作已确认断网方案；不猜隐藏参数或私有接口。 |
| 防火墙按程序参数 | 本轮 `Get-Command New-NetFirewallRule` 只读参数清单有Program、地址/端口、用户/服务等，没有ProcessId。 | 程序规则绑定可执行路径，不能称精确PID隔离；同路径其他实例也会受影响。 |
| 当前权限 | 本轮 `ctypes.windll.shell32.IsUserAnAdmin()` 返回0；此前token为Medium/Administrators deny-only。 | 无可直接增加主机网络过滤策略的提升权限。 |

6.1.1的CLI帮助不能证明所有UI绝无任何隐藏功能；本结论是**未发现受支持可执行入口**，因此不让用户盲试同类图标。此前旧工具飞行模式、smode拒绝、代理失败已充分记录，本轮不重试。

## 3. localhost是否被防火墙排除：必须区分两个层面

### 3.1 普通Windows Firewall程序规则

[微软程序规则指南](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-firewall/best-practices-configuring)支持按程序路径及端口等条件阻断出站；[New-NetFirewallRule参考](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netsecurity/new-netfirewallrule)同样提供Program条件。但这两份文档不能证明本机Win32 loopback连接一定会被该规则拦住，也未提供本题精确PID过滤承诺。

本轮没有在官方一手文档中取得“普通程序规则在当前Windows构建必定过滤/必定全豁免所有loopback”的完整契约，因此不能选择其中任一极端作为已证事实。微软另有AppContainer loopback隔离文档，其对象是UWP/AppContainer，不可直接套用到本题未打包的Win32 Emulator.exe；也不能用CheckNetIsolation开关替代普通进程隔离。

结论：可以把普通程序规则作为需要管理员的**设施实验**，但没有足够证据承诺它能切10.0.2.2→127.0.0.1 NAT；添加规则成功或公网失败均不构成通过。当前任务已有明确loopback负控要求，不建议先增加一套不确定规则再请求用户盲试。

### 3.2 Windows Filtering Platform本身可以过滤loopback

[微软Filtering condition flags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/filtering-condition-flags-)明确提供 `FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK`，适用于ALE_AUTH_CONNECT及ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT等层。因此“所有Windows过滤层都不可能阻断localhost”是不成立的。

[ALE说明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/application-layer-enforcement--ale-)支持按规范化程序文件名识别应用；[ALE层说明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/ale-layers)说明AUTH_CONNECT对应TCP connect及首个UDP/ICMP出站；[FwpmFilterAdd0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0)支持加入BLOCK过滤器。

这证明存在可设计的官方API路径；它不是New-NetFirewallRule已经承诺的行为，也不是本轮已实现的工具。

## 4. 条件化备选A：用户态WFP动态过滤工具

此节只给root可评估的最小范围，不实施、不要求安装内核驱动或第三方网络工具。[微软User Mode vs. Kernel Mode指南](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/callout-driver-programming-considerations)建议可用标准过滤完成的工作采用用户态管理程序，避免写callout驱动。

### 最小技术方案

1. 本题logs下独立辅助进程使用系统Fwpuclnt.dll；打开 `FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC` 会话，在事务内加入本题独立标记/子层及两个IPv4/IPv6 `FWP_ACTION_BLOCK` 过滤器。
2. 层只选 `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4/V6`，条件为 `FWPM_CONDITION_ALE_APP_ID` 等于本题实际Emulator.exe规范化路径，**不排除loopback**，也不只屏蔽WebDAV某个端口。这样目标是阻断该模拟器所有出站NAT连接，而非制造单服务失败。
3. 不在AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT/LISTEN/RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT层放Block，不更改全局默认策略，不阻断host其他程序。当前HDC是hdc客户端向Emulator11237监听口发起的入站连接，因此预期不命中该出站过滤。这是根据本机socket与ALE层行为作的推断，必须用HDC心跳和重连实测，不能承诺。
4. Program身份仍是路径，不是PID。预检必须确认同路径只有本题实例，实验期间禁止启动同路径其他实例；如无法保证则不能称仅影响本题。不要伪称FWPM_SESSION0.processId字段是过滤目标PID——它是管理会话客户端信息。
5. 通过动态会话生命周期恢复：显式close引擎/退出辅助进程即自动移除该会话对象；另保留可复核filter ID和按本题GUID删除的恢复操作。不得设置persistent/boot-time过滤，不禁用Windows Firewall/BFE或修改其ACL。
6. 产品负控前先结束既有应用恢复任务，断开应用旧连接。ALE为有状态过滤，不能拿旧长连接的行为猜测新连接结果；新应用请求和WFP drop记录须对应时间窗与Emulator appId。

[FWPM_SESSION0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_session0)明确动态会话结束自动删除对象。[Access Control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/access-control)说明BFE默认授管理员完整权限，普通Everyone只保证OPEN/CLASSIFY；增加过滤器还需ADD/ADD_LINK等权限。当前token不满足，必须由用户人工处理UAC/以管理员运行已审查的辅助工具，或现有合法委派；不能绕过提升、悄悄改ACL。

### 成立闸门与限制

- root须先实现并审查辅助工具及异常退出回滚；本轮没有现成已验真的命令行程序，不能用文档API当已建成的方案。
- 按v3的同endpoint在线正控→辅助工具生效→相同应用继续负控失败/活服务零到达→退出辅助工具→相同HEAD/GET恢复正控执行；加host其他程序仍可访问服务、HDC持续心跳/重连及明确的WFP drop/filter ID证据。
- 此方法实际阻断NAT出站流量，但不会自动把guest eth0设LinkDown或NetConn IsAvailable=0。若本轮要求是系统网络状态“没有默认网络”的完整离线，此方法**只能提供真实传输隔离**，不能直接替代guest系统断网；必须保留这个边界并交root按既有验收口径审查，不能悄悄降格。
- 若任一NAT HEAD/GET仍到达、HDC失联或其他host程序受影响，马上退出动态会话恢复并记录设施实验失败，不能靠改endpoint/关服务补出零请求。

故A是有官方技术依据但需要管理员与本题辅助程序开发的选项，非当前权限下可直接执行的推荐动作。

## 5. 条件化备选B：官方Emulator26的最窄外部条件

[华为官方网络教程](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-emulator-access-network#section115741355151910)明确旧模拟器虚拟Ethernet常连，断host网络或模拟器Wi-Fi不能完全断网；从26.0.0起才支持控制中心飞行模式断网仿真。[26发布说明](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-releases/deveco-studio-new-features-2600)给出工具版本26.0.0.400。该证据已在v2通过公开官方正文取得。

若不接受A的管理员/辅助工具/仅传输隔离限制，完成本题真实guest offline至少需要：

2. **被该工具实际支持且断网功能成立的guest镜像组合**。可以先新建本题API23实例验证；若旧guest不响应，则需新版官方镜像的新本题实例。不能仅凭host工具版本保证API23断网生效。

4. **若官方工具获取需许可/账户或用户允许下载**，这些前置必须真实成立。用户本轮明确不要下载，所以此处只是最小外部条件，不启动获取、不反复要求提供另一台设备，不把未来可行性当本轮完成。

L101:             printf("FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName failed (%d).\n", result);
L102:             return result;
L103:         }
L104:         else
L105:         {
L106:             printf("The Id is: %d\n", fwpApplicationByteBlob->data);
L107:         }
L108: 
L109:         return 0;
L110:     }

L24: # FwpmEngineOpen0 function (fwpmu.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The FwpmEngineOpen0 function opens a session to the filter engine.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `DWORD FwpmEngineOpen0(
L36:       [in, optional] const wchar_t             *serverName,
L37:       [in]           UINT32                    authnService,
L38:       [in, optional] SEC_WINNT_AUTH_IDENTITY_W *authIdentity,
L39:       [in, optional] const FWPM_SESSION0       *session,
L40:       [out]          HANDLE                    *engineHandle
L41:     );
L42:     `
L43: ## Parameters
L44: 
L45: `[in, optional] serverName`
L46: 
L47: Type: const wchar_t*
L48: 
L49: This value must be NULL.
L50: 
L51: `[in] authnService`
L52: 
L53: Type: UINT32
L54: 
L55: Specifies the authentication service to use. Allowed services are RPC_C_AUTHN_WINNT and RPC_C_AUTHN_DEFAULT.
L56: 
L57: `[in, optional] authIdentity`
L58: 
L59: Type: cite5†SEC_WINNT_AUTH_IDENTITY_A *
L60: 
L61: The authentication and authorization credentials for accessing the filter engine. This pointer is optional and can be NULL. If this pointer is NULL, the calling thread's credentials are used.
L62: `[in, optional] session`
L63: 
L64: Type: cite6†FWPM_SESSION0 *
L65: 
L66: Session-specific parameters for the session being opened. This pointer is optional and can be NULL.
L67: 
L68: `[out] engineHandle`
L69: 
L70: Type: HANDLE*
L71: 
L72: Handle for the open session to the filter engine.
L73: ## Return value
L74: 
L75: Type: DWORD
L76: 
L77: Return code/value  | Description
L78: --- | ---
L79: 
L80: ERROR_SUCCESS
L81: 0
L82:  | The session was started successfully.
L83: 
L84: FWP_E_ALREADY_EXISTS
L85: 0x80320009
L86:  | A session with the specified sessionKey is already opened.
L87: 
L88: FWP_E_* error code
L89: 0x80320001—0x80320039
L90:  | A Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) specific error. See cite7†WFP Error Codes for details.
L91: 
L92: RPC_* error code
L93: 0x80010001—0x80010122
L94:  | Failure to communicate with the remote or local firewall engine.
L95: ## Remarks
L96: 
L97: A user application must call FwpmEngineOpen0 to obtain a handle for open session to the filter engine before adding or removing any filter objects. A handle for an open session to the filter engine is also required for most of the other Windows Filtering Platform management functions.
L98: 
L99: The session is automatically closed when the program ends. To explicitly close a session, call cite8†FwpmEngineClose0 .
L100: If session.flags is set to FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC, any WFP objects added during the session are automatically deleted when the session ends. If the session is not dynamic, the caller needs to explicitly delete all WFP objects added during the session.
L101: 
L102: The caller needs cite9†FWPM_ACTRL_OPEN access to the filter engine. See cite10†Access Control for more information.
L103: 
L104: FwpmEngineOpen0 is intended for use in non-impersonated mode only.
L105: FwpmEngineOpen0 is a specific implementation of FwpmEngineOpen. See cite11†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows for more information.
L106: #### Examples
L107: The following C++ example uses FwpmEngineOpen0 to open a filter session.
L108: 
L109:     `// Open a session to the filter engine
L110: 
L111:     HANDLE    engineHandle = NULL;
L112:     DWORD    result = ERROR_SUCCESS;
L113: 
L114:     printf("Opening the filter engine.\n");
L115: 
L116:     result = FwpmEngineOpen0(
L117:         NULL,
L118:         RPC_C_AUTHN_WINNT,
L119:         NULL,
L120:         NULL,
L121:         &engineHandle );
L122: 
L123:     if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)
L124:         printf("FwpmEngineOpen0 failed. Return value: %d.\n", result);
L125:     else
L126:         printf("Filter engine opened successfully.\n");
L127: 
L128:     `

L130: 
L131: Requirement  | Value
L132: --- | ---
L133: Minimum supported client  | Windows Vista [desktop apps only]
L134: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server 2008 [desktop apps only]
L135: Target Platform  | Windows
L136: Header  | fwpmu.h
L137: Library  | Fwpuclnt.lib
L138: DLL  | Fwpuclnt.dll

L24: # FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 structure (fwpmtypes.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 structure expresses a filter condition that must be true for the action to be taken.
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `typedef struct FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0_ {
L37:       GUID                 fieldKey;
L38:       FWP_MATCH_TYPE       matchType;
L39:       FWP_CONDITION_VALUE0 conditionValue;
L40:     } FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0;
L41:     `
L42: ## Members
L43: 
L44: `fieldKey`
L45: 
L46: GUID of the field to be tested. The available keys are listed under cite5†Filtering Condition Identifiers .
L47: 
L48: `matchType`
L49: 
L50: A cite6†FWP_MATCH_TYPE value that specifies the type of match to be performed.
L51: 
L52: `conditionValue`
L53: 
L54: A cite7†FWP_CONDITION_VALUE0 structure that contains the value to match the field against.
L55: ## Remarks
L56: 
L57: Field GUIDs are only unique within a layer, so both the field GUID and the layer GUID are required to uniquely identify a field.
L58: 
L59: The data type of
L60: 
L61: cite6†FWP_MATCH_TYPE for detailed compatibility rules.
L62: 
L63: FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 is a specific implementation of FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION. See cite8†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows for more information.
L64: #### Examples
L65: The following C++ example shows how to initialize and add conditions to a filter.
L66: 
L67:     `#include <windows.h>
L68:     #include <fwpmu.h>
L69:     #include <stdio.h>
L70: 
L71:     #pragma comment(lib, "Fwpuclnt.lib")
L72: 
L73:     // Some application to use for filter testing.
L74:     #define FILE0_PATH L"C:\\Program Files\\AppDirectory\\SomeApplication.exe"
L75: 
L76:     void main()
L77:     {
L78:         FWP_BYTE_BLOB *fwpApplicationByteBlob;
L79:         FWPM_FILTER0 fwpFilter;
L80:         FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 fwpConditions[4];
L81:         int conCount = 0;
L82:         DWORD result = ERROR_SUCCESS;
L83: 
L84:         fwpApplicationByteBlob = (FWP_BYTE_BLOB*) malloc(sizeof(FWP_BYTE_BLOB));
L85: 
L86:         printf("Retrieving application identifier for filter testing.\n");
L87:         result = FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName0(FILE0_PATH, &fwpApplicationByteBlob);
L88:         if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)
L89:         {
L90:             printf("FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName failed (%d).\n", result);
L91:             return;
L92:         }
L93:           // Application identifier filter condition.
L94:           fwpConditions[conCount].fieldKey = FWPM_CONDITION_ALE_APP_ID;
L95:           fwpConditions[conCount].matchType = FWP_MATCH_EQUAL;
L96:           fwpConditions[conCount].conditionValue.type = FWP_BYTE_BLOB_TYPE;
L97:           fwpConditions[conCount].conditionValue.byteBlob = fwpApplicationByteBlob;
L98: 
L99:           ++conCount;
L100: 
L101:           // TCP protocol filter condition
L102:           fwpConditions[conCount].fieldKey = FWPM_CONDITION_IP_PROTOCOL;
L103:           fwpConditions[conCount].matchType = FWP_MATCH_EQUAL;
L104:           fwpConditions[conCount].conditionValue.type = FWP_UINT8;
L105:           fwpConditions[conCount].conditionValue.uint8 = IPPROTO_TCP;
L106: 
L107:           ++conCount;
L108: 
L109:           // Add conditions and condition count to a filter.
L110:           memset(&fwpFilter, 0, sizeof(FWPM_FILTER0));
L111: 
L112:           fwpFilter.numFilterConditions = conCount;
L113:           if (conCount > 0)
L114:             fwpFilter.filterCondition = fwpConditions;
L115:           // Finish initializing filter...
L116: 
L117:         return;
L118:     }
L119: 
L120:     `

L24: # FWPM_FILTER0 structure (fwpmtypes.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The FWPM_FILTER0 structure stores the state associated with a filter.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `typedef struct FWPM_FILTER0_ {
L36:       GUID                   filterKey;
L37:       FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0     displayData;
L38:       UINT32                 flags;
L39:       GUID                   *providerKey;
L40:       FWP_BYTE_BLOB          providerData;
L41:       GUID                   layerKey;
L42:       GUID                   subLayerKey;
L43:       FWP_VALUE0             weight;
L44:       UINT32                 numFilterConditions;
L45:       FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 *filterCondition;
L46:       FWPM_ACTION0           action;
L47:       union {
L48:         UINT64 rawContext;
L49:         GUID   providerContextKey;
L50:       };
L51:       GUID                   *reserved;
L52:       UINT64                 filterId;
L53:       FWP_VALUE0             effectiveWeight;
L54:     } FWPM_FILTER0;
L55:     `
L56: ## Members
L57: 
L58: `filterKey`
L59: 
L60: Uniquely identifies the session.
L61: 
L62: If the GUID is initialized to zero in the call to cite5†FwpmFilterAdd0 , the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) will generate one.
L63: 
L64: `displayData`
L65: 
L66: A cite6†FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 structure that contains human-readable annotations associated with the filter. The name member of the FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 structure is required.
L67: 
L68: `flags`
L69: 
L70: A combination of the following values.
L71: 
L72: Filter flag  | Meaning
L73: --- | ---
L74: 
L75: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_NONE**
L76:  | Default.
L77: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**
L78:  | Filter is persistent, that is, it survives across BFE stop/start. **Note**  This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**.
L79: 
L80: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**
L81:  | Filter is enforced at boot-time, even before BFE starts. **Note**  This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**.
L82: 
L83: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT**
L84:  | Filter references a provider context.
L85: 
L86: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT**
L87:  | Clear filter action right.
L88: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERMIT_IF_CALLOUT_UNREGISTERED**
L89:  | If the callout is not registered, the filter is treated as a permit filter. **Note**  This flag can be set only if the **action** type is **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_TERMINATING** or **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_UNKNOWN**.
L90: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_DISABLED**
L91:  | Filter is disabled. A provider's filters are disabled when the BFE starts if the provider has no associated Windows service name, or if the associated service is not set to auto-start. **Note**  This flag cannot be set when adding new filters. It can only be returned by BFE when getting or enumerating filters.
L92: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_INDEXED**
L93:  | Filter is indexed to help enable faster lookup during classification. **Note**  Available only in Windows 8 and Windows Server 2012.
L94: 
L95: `providerKey`
L96: 
L97: Optional GUID of the policy provider that manages this filter. See cite7†Built-in Provider Identifiers for a list of predefined policy providers.
L98: 
L99: `providerData`
L100: 
L101: A cite8†FWP_BYTE_BLOB structure that contains optional provider-specific data used by providers to store additional context information with the object.
L102: 
L103: `layerKey`
L104: GUID of the layer where the filter resides. See cite9†Filtering Layer Identifiers for a list of possible values.
L105: 
L106: `subLayerKey`
L107: 
L108: GUID of the sub-layer where the filter resides. See cite10†Filtering Sub-Layer Identifiers for a list of built-in sub-layers.
L109: 
L110: If this is set to IID_NULL, the filter is added to the default sublayer.
L111: 
L112: `weight`
L113: A cite11†FWP_VALUE0 structure that specifies the weight of the filter. The weight indicates the priority of the filter, where higher-numbered weights have higher priorities (and will be evaluated before lower-weighted filters).
L114: 
L115: Possible type values for weight are as follows.
L116: 
L117: **weight** type  | Meaning
L118: --- | ---
L119: 
L120: **FWP_UINT64**
L121:  | BFE will use the supplied value as the filter's weight.
L122: **FWP_UINT8**
L123: 0–15
L124:  | BFE will use the supplied value as a weight range index and will compute the filter's weight in that range. See cite12†Filter Weight Assignment for more information.
L125: 
L126: **FWP_EMPTY**
L127:  | BFE will automatically assign a weight based on the filter conditions.
L128: 
L129: See cite13†Filter Weight Identifiers for built-in constants that may be used to compute the filter weight.
L130: 
L131: `numFilterConditions`
L132: 
L133: Number of filter conditions.
L134: 
L135: `filterCondition`
L136: Array of cite14†FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 structures that contain all the filtering conditions. All must be true for the action to be performed. In other words, the conditions are evaluated using the AND operator. If no conditions are specified, the action is always performed.
L137: 
L138: **Note**  In Windows 7 and Windows Server 2008 R2, consecutive conditions with the same fieldKey will be evaluated using the OR operator.
L139: 
L140: 
L141: 
L142: `action`
L143: A cite15†FWPM_ACTION0 structure that specifies the action to be performed if all the filter conditions are true.
L144: 
L145: `rawContext`
L146: 
L147: Available when the filter does not have provider context information, that is, flags does not contain FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT. See cite16†Filter Context Identifiers for a list of built-in possible values.
L148: 
L149: The rawContext is placed 'as is' in the context member of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.
L150: 
L151: `providerContextKey`
L152: Available when the filter has provider context information, that is, flags contains FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT. See cite17†Built-in Provider Context Identifiers for a list of predefined policy provider contexts.
L153: 
L154: The LUID of the provider context specified by the providerContextKey is used to fill in the context member of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.
L155: 
L156: `reserved`
L157: 
L158: Reserved for system use.
L159: 
L160: `filterId`
L161: LUID identifying the filter. This is also the LUID of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.
L162: 
L163: `effectiveWeight`
L164: 
L165: An cite11†FWP_VALUE0 structure that contains the weight assigned to FWPS_FILTER0, which is documented in the WDK.
L166: ## Remarks
L167: 
L168: The first ten members of this structure contain information supplied when adding objects.
L169:

+## 7. 按root追加要求：无驱动C#辅助设施的最小实现合同 v4.1

+
+### 7.1 最窄P/Invoke声明
+
+```csharp
+using System;
+using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
+
+internal static class WfpNative {
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmEngineOpen0(IntPtr serverName,
+        uint authnService, IntPtr authIdentity, IntPtr session,
+        out IntPtr engineHandle);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true, CharSet = CharSet.Unicode)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName0(string fileName,
+        out IntPtr appId);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionBegin0(IntPtr engineHandle, uint flags);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmFilterAdd0(IntPtr engineHandle,
+        IntPtr filter, IntPtr securityDescriptor, out ulong filterId);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionCommit0(IntPtr engineHandle);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionAbort0(IntPtr engineHandle);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern uint FwpmEngineClose0(IntPtr engineHandle);
+    [DllImport("Fwpuclnt.dll", ExactSpelling = true)]
+    internal static extern void FwpmFreeMemory0(ref IntPtr memory);
+}
+```
+
+管理函数返回DWORD错误码，逐次检查0/nonzero；不能用Marshal.GetLastWin32Error替代返回值。上述IntPtr是对明确原生结构的指针，不是省略ABI校验的许可。serverName/authIdentity使用NULL，authnService取官方RPC_C_AUTHN_WINNT，session必须为完整FWPM_SESSION0且flags=1（DYNAMIC）。AppId使用官方函数取得的FWP_BYTE_BLOB指针，不手工拼文件路径字节；最后按官方要求FwpmFreeMemory0释放。
+
+一手签名：[EngineOpen0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmengineopen0)、[GetAppIdFromFileName0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmgetappidfromfilename0)、[FilterAdd0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0)。EngineOpen0文档明确进程结束自动关闭会话；动态会话中的对象随结束自动删除，并非仅依赖正常finally执行。

+### 7.2 必要结构与过滤器内容
+
+| 原生类型 | 托管实现要点 | 本辅助工具实际使用 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 | 两个UTF-16字符串指针 | 本题名称/说明，所有非托管字符串在添加完成前保持有效。 |
+| FWPM_SESSION0 | Guid、displayData、uint flags/timeout/processId、SID/username指针、32位BOOL；按x64原生对齐 | 只填displayData和DYNAMIC，其余清零，不能用processId绑定被过滤进程。 |
+| FWP_BYTE_BLOB | uint size + 对齐后的IntPtr data | 使用GetAppId函数分配的blob，不修改。 |
+| FWP_VALUE0 / FWP_CONDITION_VALUE0 | 32位type + 原生union；x64指针union按8字节对齐 | weight取FWP_EMPTY；条件type=FWP_BYTE_BLOB_TYPE、union保存上述blob指针。 |
+| FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 | Guid fieldKey、32位matchType、conditionValue | 唯一条件APP_ID / EQUAL / appBlob，避免多余endpoint限定。 |
+| FWPM_ACTION0 | uint type + GUID union | type=FWP_ACTION_BLOCK（0x1001），其余清零，不用callout。 |
+| FWPM_FILTER0 | 完整原生定义，尤其action后的16字节rawContext/providerContext union、reserved指针、filterId/effectiveWeight不能省略 | 两个不同filterKey；每个numFilterConditions=1；flags=0，无持久化/启动过滤；weight=EMPTY。 |

+管理函数返回DWORD错误码，逐次检查0/nonzero；不能用Marshal.GetLastWin32Error替代返回值。上述IntPtr是对明确原生结构的指针，不是省略ABI校验的许可。serverName/authIdentity使用NULL，authnService取官方RPC_C_AUTHN_WINNT，session必须为完整FWPM_SESSION0且flags=1（DYNAMIC）。AppId使用官方函数取得的FWP_BYTE_BLOB指针，不手工拼文件路径字节；最后按官方要求FwpmFreeMemory0释放。

+一手签名：[EngineOpen0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmengineopen0)、[GetAppIdFromFileName0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmgetappidfromfilename0)、[FilterAdd0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0)。EngineOpen0文档明确进程结束自动关闭会话；动态会话中的对象随结束自动删除，并非仅依赖正常finally执行。
+
+### 7.2 必要结构与过滤器内容
+
+| 原生类型 | 托管实现要点 | 本辅助工具实际使用 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 | 两个UTF-16字符串指针 | 本题名称/说明，所有非托管字符串在添加完成前保持有效。 |
+| FWPM_SESSION0 | Guid、displayData、uint flags/timeout/processId、SID/username指针、32位BOOL；按x64原生对齐 | 只填displayData和DYNAMIC，其余清零，不能用processId绑定被过滤进程。 |
+| FWP_BYTE_BLOB | uint size + 对齐后的IntPtr data | 使用GetAppId函数分配的blob，不修改。 |
+| FWP_VALUE0 / FWP_CONDITION_VALUE0 | 32位type + 原生union；x64指针union按8字节对齐 | weight取FWP_EMPTY；条件type=FWP_BYTE_BLOB_TYPE、union保存上述blob指针。 |
+| FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 | Guid fieldKey、32位matchType、conditionValue | 唯一条件APP_ID / EQUAL / appBlob，避免多余endpoint限定。 |
+| FWPM_ACTION0 | uint type + GUID union | type=FWP_ACTION_BLOCK（0x1001），其余清零，不用callout。 |
+| FWPM_FILTER0 | 完整原生定义，尤其action后的16字节rawContext/providerContext union、reserved指针、filterId/effectiveWeight不能省略 | 两个不同filterKey；每个numFilterConditions=1；flags=0，无持久化/启动过滤；weight=EMPTY。 |
+
+最窄版可将subLayerKey置Guid.Empty，官方FWPM_FILTER0文档允许使用默认子层；无需额外provider、服务或callout注册。若实现选择本题独立子层，则只增加同一动态会话内的SubLayerAdd0，不改系统子层/ACL。两条过滤器在同一事务内全部成功才commit；任一失败abort并close，不能半启用IPv4或IPv6后继续测试。
+
+[FILTER_CONDITION0官方示例](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter_condition0)直接示范APP_ID + EQUAL + BYTE_BLOB；[FILTER0官方定义](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter0)给出完整布局、默认子层和自动权重。实现者应在任何BFE写调用之前核对Marshal.SizeOf/OffsetOf与原生x64布局，不能把32位示例偏移照搬到64位；先完成仅编译/布局检查，再由root决定管理员执行。

+本轮从微软维护的通用[Windows SDK头文件fwpmu.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/fwpmu.h)只读核对三个GUID（不是应用来源代码）：
+
+- AUTH_CONNECT_V4：`c38d57d1-05a7-4c33-904f-7fbceee60e82`。
+- AUTH_CONNECT_V6：`4a72393b-319f-44bc-84c3-ba54dcb3b6b4`。
+- CONDITION_ALE_APP_ID：`d78e1e87-8644-4ea5-9437-d809ecefc971`。
+

+
+### 7.3 HDC边界、人工条件和不能承诺的部分
+
+- **HDC保护依据**：只在AUTH_CONNECT层按Emulator appId过滤主动出站。当前hdc客户端主动连接Emulator的host11237监听口，其AUTH_CONNECT身份是hdc进程，Emulator在RECV_ACCEPT接收；现有HDC连接及其返回流量不因“是loopback”就必然匹配该Emulator出站策略。不要增加“全host loopback block”或RECV_ACCEPT block。
+- **不足**：WFP策略变化会导致ALE连接重新授权；具体模拟器控制链是否另建主动出站socket、以及内部NAT是否归于同一appId，尚无本题已执行证明。必须在真正隔离后持续HDC心跳、一次合法断开重连、UI树/操作，并证明NAT同路径负控失败。HDC中断立即让辅助进程退出触发动态回滚；外部恢复进程不依赖HDC。

+- **当前成熟度**：只有官方API可行性、编译器存在和最小设计合同；没有辅助程序、布局实测、过滤器写入或NAT/HDC实验。它是有界的设施研发方案，**不能保证替代Emulator26，也不能让guest网络管理器必然报告系统offline**。root若采用，应另行分配本题辅助工具实现/验证所有权，并维持生产冻结；若要求即用且guest状态真正离线，仍需第5节官方26能力条件。

# vg-spec1 scoped WFP test helper

This is test infrastructure, not application code. It has been compiled and checked without administrator rights. **No filter has been enabled by the implementation role.** An elevated run, NAT failure/recovery and HDC continuity still require separate approval and independent testing. A BLOCKED acknowledgment proves filter configuration, not packet drops, guest LinkDown or R27 success.

## Fixed scope

- Only `D:\HarmonyDev\vg-spec1-isolated-emulator61\Emulator.exe` is allowed. The original installed Emulator paths are never accepted as targets.
- Exactly one readable process at that path, the specified PID and exact UTC StartTime, expected binary SHA256, command line `-instance VgSpec1ManualOffline`, explicit `-hvdport 11237`, and `-path` equal to the specified instance root are required.
- Instance root and run/control directory must be existing children of `D:\HCUP\vg-spec1\logs\`. Reparse points/junctions in those paths are rejected. No control message can change any target parameter.
- WFP matches the executable **APP_ID/path**, not PID. PID/StartTime/instance checks are user-mode guards. Another process at the same copied path would temporarily share the path condition until the next guard check; starting it during the experiment is prohibited. Detection closes the session and exits with an error. The original executable's other instances do not share this copied path.
- Only two outbound layers are used: ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4 and V6. Each filter has exactly one EQUAL/BYTE_BLOB ALE_APP_ID condition and BLOCK action, flags zero, and a new owned nonpersistent sublayer. No loopback exception, endpoint/port limitation, RECEIVE/LISTEN filter, kernel driver, Windows Firewall setting, BFE/ACL change or global audit collection is used.

## Build and read-only check (ordinary terminal)

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Build-Guard.ps1'
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/bin/VgSpec1WfpGuard.exe' --check
```

The build script loads the required Harmony environment, invokes the installed x64 .NET Framework compiler with warnings as errors, and runs only `--check`. It writes each attempt's compiler/check output under `logs/development-round-03/wfp-build/` and a source/binary SHA256 manifest under `bin/`. No downloads, NuGet packages or new compiler are needed. Rebuilding changes the executable hash; use the final reviewed manifest.

No arguments also means check. This mode only reads ABI sizes/offsets, administrator-token status, fixed file presence/hash and, if all target options are supplied, process guards. It never calls EngineOpen or any WFP API. The `nativeWfpCalls:0` field records that code path; it is not a trace of an elevated experiment. If the copied tool does not exist, basic check still succeeds and reports its absence; live target validation remains unverified.

An optional check with `--target-pid`, `--target-start-utc`, `--target-sha256`, and `--instance-root` performs the same read-only target guard. Exact StartTime should come from `(Get-Process -Id <PID>).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString('o')`. No target is guessed or created by this helper.

## User's manual elevated entry (do not run during preparation)

The root/verification role first copies the complete official installed emulator tool directory into the fixed isolated directory, then starts only the reviewed task instance using an explicit task-local `-path` and port. This helper does not copy or start it. A fresh run directory and 32 lowercase hexadecimal nonce must be prepared by the controller. Do not reuse a directory containing `status.json` or `helper.lock`.

The **user** opens an administrator PowerShell console and runs the reviewed entry with actual PID/time/hash/root values:

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Start-GuardManually.ps1' `
  -TargetPid <ACTUAL_PID> -TargetStartUtc '<EXACT_UTC_STARTTIME>' `
  -TargetSha256 '<EXPECTED_64_LOWERCASE_HEX>' `
  -InstanceRoot 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<reviewed-instance-root>' `
  -RunDirectory 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<fresh-run-directory>' `
  -RunNonce '<32_LOWERCASE_HEX>' -MaxSeconds 1200 -MaxBlockSeconds 600
```

This script requires an already elevated console and checks the built EXE and source hashes. It never invokes UAC/RunAs. Do not substitute paths or omit independent review. `--serve` refuses unelevated callers before any WFP call. It starts **IDLE_UNBLOCKED**, with no engine open and no filters. Only an accepted block request opens the dynamic engine and adds objects.

Total runtime defaults to 1200 seconds, hard range 30–1800. Each continuous block defaults to 600 seconds, hard range 5–900, and can never extend past the total deadline. A successful repeated block is idempotent and cannot extend its absolute block deadline. Monotonic time enforces these limits. The watchdog checks target/lease/deadlines once per second; target binary size/mtime is checked each tick and full SHA256 is forced every ten seconds and immediately before blocking. A changed/unreadable target, second same-path process, stale controller or deadline causes cleanup, an explicit error status and exit. Startup allows at most 45 seconds for the first fresh request.

An independent background watchdog checks the same monotonic total/lease/block deadlines every 250 ms. If a synchronous BFE/WMI call prevents the normal close/error path for more than three seconds past a deadline, it terminates the management process with FailFast so Windows dynamic-session/RPC cleanup can run. That abnormal exit and any stale status must fail the facility gate; it cannot be treated as a normal acknowledgment. No global audit policy is changed. Actual crash/rundown recovery is still an elevated validation item.

## Control protocol (ordinary controller, no privileges)

The only input is `<RunDirectory>/request.json`, strict UTF-8 JSON, at most 4096 bytes, with exactly these five fields:

```json
{"nonce":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","sequence":1,"operation":"unblock","createdUtc":"2026-10-17T10:00:00.0000000Z","expiresUtc":"2026-10-17T10:00:10.0000000Z"}
```

Use the actual nonce and current UTC times. Allowed operations are exactly `block`, `unblock`, `exit`. Sequence is a strictly increasing positive integer. Creation can be at most two seconds in the future or fifteen seconds old; expiration must be later than creation/current time and at most fifteen seconds after creation. Wrong nonce/sequence/fields/operation/expired messages are rejected and do not renew the lease. The old unchanged file never renews it. Emit a new atomic replacement every three seconds with a ten-second lease while the test is active, including while unblocked. On lost lease the helper closes and exits **ERROR_UNBLOCKED**, code 3; that must fail the facility gate, never silently become a passing cancellation case. A new nonce cannot be adopted by the existing helper.

For individual requests, the supplied ordinary-user writer performs atomic replacement:

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Send-GuardRequest.ps1' `
  -RunDirectory '<SAME_RUN_DIRECTORY>' -RunNonce '<SAME_NONCE>' `
  -Sequence 1 -Operation unblock -LeaseSeconds 10
```

The controller's next request uses sequence 2, and so forth. A writer's output is not a helper acknowledgment. Wait for matching nonce/accepted sequence and the required state in `status.json`; keep auditing that heartbeat and the unchanged deadline/filter IDs.

`status.json` is replaced atomically once per tick and after termination:

- `schemaVersion`, `task`, `nonce`, `state`, `active` (boolean), `helperPid`, `timestampUtc`.
- `lastAcceptedSequence`, nullable `lastAcceptedUtc`, `requestExpiresUtc`, `totalDeadlineUtc`, nullable `blockDeadlineUtc`.
- `target`: fixed `path`, `pid`, exact `startTimeUtc`, `sha256`, fixed `instance`, `instanceRoot`, `hdcPort` (string `11237`), `guardOk` and `lastGuardUtc` (last successful guard).
- `filters`: empty before/after block; while BLOCKED exactly two objects with `id` (decimal string), `key`, `layerGuid`, `layerName`, `verified:true`.
- `nativeEngineOpen`, `sessionGuid`, `subLayerGuid`, nullable `terminationReason`, `auditMode:not_enabled`, `proof:filter_configuration_only`.

State literals are `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, `BLOCKED`, `EXITED_UNBLOCKED`, `ERROR_UNBLOCKED`, and exceptional `ERROR_CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED`. The last state means NativeClose failed: never claim recovery from that snapshot; the process exits with code 4 so Windows RPC rundown can clean its dynamic objects, followed by independent recovery verification. The normal error exit code is 3. `terminationReason` is null while running and records exit_request/console_cancel or the specific failed guard/deadline/lease/API cause at termination.

`helper.jsonl` records ready, armed, control accepted/rejected, each DWORD-returning native call result, filter ID/layer/key, exact target path/hash, APP_ID blob hash, session/sublayer GUID and cleanup. Pre-commit and post-commit GetById verify identity, owned sublayer, flags, exact single APP_ID condition/type/match/blob and BLOCK action. If same-transaction GetById cannot read newly added filters, the transaction is aborted and the engine closed: there is no fallback that skips this verification. That visibility and all API behavior remain untested until an approved elevated run. No WFP net-event/drop audit has been enabled or claimed.

## Recovery

1. Send a current nonce/sequence `unblock`, then check matching `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, active false, engine false, empty filters, and the real NAT recovery control.
2. Send current `exit`, or press Ctrl+C in the manually opened helper console. Both close the dynamic session and terminate.
3. If the controller/HDC is unavailable, use the helper console's Ctrl+C. As a last local recovery, the user may terminate only the recorded helper PID after checking its executable path/StartTime. Terminating this management process ends the dynamic WFP session; do not kill unrelated Emulator or HDC processes.
4. Unexpected process death also ends the dynamic session by the official WFP lifecycle contract. A stale status file is not a live acknowledgment; independently confirm restored same-endpoint HEAD/GET. There are no persistent/boot-time rules to restore, no global defaults were changed, and no broad cleanup rule should be run.

The independent sequence remains online positive control → scoped block plus same-endpoint failure/zero arrivals and host-service liveness → three cancellation cases with full evidence → unblock/exit and same-endpoint recovery. Check HDC heartbeat and lawful reconnection throughout. A guest may still report eth0/NetConn available: this helper targets transmission isolation, not the guest network-manager state. Do not report R27 passed until the root agent reviews the independent evidence and this boundary.

## Primary references

Native types/constants/GUIDs are based on Microsoft's [WinSDK fwpmtypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwpmtypes.h), [fwptypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwptypes.h), [fwpmu.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/fwpmu.h) and [rpcdce.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/rpcdce.h). Relevant APIs: [EngineOpen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmengineopen0), [FilterAdd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0), [FilterGetById](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfiltergetbyid0), [SubLayerAdd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmsublayeradd0), [Object Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/object-management). The implementation report records actual compiler/layout evidence separately from these API contracts.

# vg-spec1 scoped WFP test helper

This is test infrastructure, not application code. It has been compiled and checked without administrator rights. **No filter has been enabled by the implementation role.** An elevated run, NAT failure/recovery and HDC continuity still require separate approval and independent testing. A BLOCKED acknowledgment proves filter configuration, not packet drops, guest LinkDown or R27 success.

## Fixed scope

- Only `D:\HarmonyDev\vg-spec1-isolated-emulator61\Emulator.exe` is allowed. The original installed Emulator paths are never accepted as targets.
- Exactly one readable process at that path, the specified PID and exact UTC StartTime, expected binary SHA256, command line `-instance VgSpec1ManualOffline`, explicit `-hvdport 11237`, and `-path` equal to the specified instance root are required.
- Instance root and run/control directory must be existing children of `D:\HCUP\vg-spec1\logs\`. Reparse points/junctions in those paths are rejected. No control message can change any target parameter.
- WFP matches the executable **APP_ID/path**, not PID. PID/StartTime/instance checks are user-mode guards. Another process at the same copied path would temporarily share the path condition until the next guard check; starting it during the experiment is prohibited. Detection closes the session and exits with an error. The original executable's other instances do not share this copied path.
- Only two outbound layers are used: ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4 and V6. Each filter has exactly one EQUAL/BYTE_BLOB ALE_APP_ID condition and BLOCK action, flags zero, and a new owned nonpersistent sublayer. No loopback exception, endpoint/port limitation, RECEIVE/LISTEN filter, kernel driver, Windows Firewall setting, BFE/ACL change or global audit collection is used.

## Build and read-only check (ordinary terminal)

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Build-Guard.ps1'
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/bin/VgSpec1WfpGuard.exe' --check
```

The build script loads the required Harmony environment, invokes the installed x64 .NET Framework compiler with warnings as errors, and runs only `--check`. It writes each attempt's compiler/check output under `logs/development-round-03/wfp-build/` and a source/binary SHA256 manifest under `bin/`. No downloads, NuGet packages or new compiler are needed. Rebuilding changes the executable hash; use the final reviewed manifest.

No arguments also means check. This mode only reads ABI sizes/offsets, administrator-token status, fixed file presence/hash and, if all target options are supplied, process guards. It never calls EngineOpen or any WFP API. The `nativeWfpCalls:0` field records that code path; it is not a trace of an elevated experiment. If the copied tool does not exist, basic check still succeeds and reports its absence; live target validation remains unverified.

An optional check with `--target-pid`, `--target-start-utc`, `--target-sha256`, and `--instance-root` performs the same read-only target guard. Exact StartTime should come from `(Get-Process -Id <PID>).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString('o')`. No target is guessed or created by this helper.

## User's manual elevated entry (do not run during preparation)

The root/verification role first copies the complete official installed emulator tool directory into the fixed isolated directory, then starts only the reviewed task instance using an explicit task-local `-path` and port. This helper does not copy or start it. A fresh run directory and 32 lowercase hexadecimal nonce must be prepared by the controller. Do not reuse a directory containing `status.json` or `helper.lock`.

The **user** opens an administrator PowerShell console and runs the reviewed entry with actual PID/time/hash/root values:

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Start-GuardManually.ps1' `
  -TargetPid <ACTUAL_PID> -TargetStartUtc '<EXACT_UTC_STARTTIME>' `
  -TargetSha256 '<EXPECTED_64_LOWERCASE_HEX>' `
  -InstanceRoot 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<reviewed-instance-root>' `
  -RunDirectory 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<fresh-run-directory>' `
  -RunNonce '<32_LOWERCASE_HEX>' -MaxSeconds 1200 -MaxBlockSeconds 600
```

This script requires an already elevated console and checks the built EXE and source hashes. It never invokes UAC/RunAs. Do not substitute paths or omit independent review. `--serve` refuses unelevated callers before any WFP call. It starts **IDLE_UNBLOCKED**, with no engine open and no filters. Only an accepted block request opens the dynamic engine and adds objects.

Total runtime defaults to 1200 seconds, hard range 30–1800. Each continuous block defaults to 600 seconds, hard range 5–900, and can never extend past the total deadline. A successful repeated block is idempotent and cannot extend its absolute block deadline. Monotonic time enforces these limits. The watchdog checks target/lease/deadlines once per second; target binary size/mtime is checked each tick and full SHA256 is forced every ten seconds and immediately before blocking. A changed/unreadable target, second same-path process, stale controller or deadline causes cleanup, an explicit error status and exit. Startup allows at most 45 seconds for the first fresh request.

An independent background watchdog checks the same monotonic total/lease/block deadlines every 250 ms. If a synchronous BFE/WMI call prevents the normal close/error path for more than three seconds past a deadline, it terminates the management process with FailFast so Windows dynamic-session/RPC cleanup can run. That abnormal exit and any stale status must fail the facility gate; it cannot be treated as a normal acknowledgment. No global audit policy is changed. Actual crash/rundown recovery is still an elevated validation item.

## Control protocol (ordinary controller, no privileges)

The only input is `<RunDirectory>/request.json`, strict UTF-8 JSON, at most 4096 bytes, with exactly these five fields:

```json
{"nonce":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","sequence":1,"operation":"unblock","createdUtc":"2026-10-17T10:00:00.0000000Z","expiresUtc":"2026-10-17T10:00:10.0000000Z"}
```

Use the actual nonce and current UTC times. Allowed operations are exactly `block`, `unblock`, `exit`. Sequence is a strictly increasing positive integer. Creation can be at most two seconds in the future or fifteen seconds old; expiration must be later than creation/current time and at most fifteen seconds after creation. Wrong nonce/sequence/fields/operation/expired messages are rejected and do not renew the lease. The old unchanged file never renews it. Emit a new atomic replacement every three seconds with a ten-second lease while the test is active, including while unblocked. On lost lease the helper closes and exits **ERROR_UNBLOCKED**, code 3; that must fail the facility gate, never silently become a passing cancellation case. A new nonce cannot be adopted by the existing helper.

For individual requests, the supplied ordinary-user writer performs atomic replacement:

```powershell
& 'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Send-GuardRequest.ps1' `
  -RunDirectory '<SAME_RUN_DIRECTORY>' -RunNonce '<SAME_NONCE>' `
  -Sequence 1 -Operation unblock -LeaseSeconds 10
```

The controller's next request uses sequence 2, and so forth. A writer's output is not a helper acknowledgment. Wait for matching nonce/accepted sequence and the required state in `status.json`; keep auditing that heartbeat and the unchanged deadline/filter IDs.

`status.json` is replaced atomically once per tick and after termination:

- `schemaVersion`, `task`, `nonce`, `state`, `active` (boolean), `helperPid`, `timestampUtc`.
- `lastAcceptedSequence`, nullable `lastAcceptedUtc`, `requestExpiresUtc`, `totalDeadlineUtc`, nullable `blockDeadlineUtc`.
- `target`: fixed `path`, `pid`, exact `startTimeUtc`, `sha256`, fixed `instance`, `instanceRoot`, `hdcPort` (string `11237`), `guardOk` and `lastGuardUtc` (last successful guard).
- `filters`: empty before/after block; while BLOCKED exactly two objects with `id` (decimal string), `key`, `layerGuid`, `layerName`, `verified:true`.
- `nativeEngineOpen`, `sessionGuid`, `subLayerGuid`, nullable `terminationReason`, `auditMode:not_enabled`, `proof:filter_configuration_only`.

State literals are `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, `BLOCKED`, `EXITED_UNBLOCKED`, `ERROR_UNBLOCKED`, and exceptional `ERROR_CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED`. The last state means NativeClose failed: never claim recovery from that snapshot; the process exits with code 4 so Windows RPC rundown can clean its dynamic objects, followed by independent recovery verification. The normal error exit code is 3. `terminationReason` is null while running and records exit_request/console_cancel or the specific failed guard/deadline/lease/API cause at termination.

`helper.jsonl` records ready, armed, control accepted/rejected, each DWORD-returning native call result, filter ID/layer/key, exact target path/hash, APP_ID blob hash, session/sublayer GUID and cleanup. Pre-commit and post-commit GetById verify identity, owned sublayer, flags, exact single APP_ID condition/type/match/blob and BLOCK action. If same-transaction GetById cannot read newly added filters, the transaction is aborted and the engine closed: there is no fallback that skips this verification. That visibility and all API behavior remain untested until an approved elevated run. No WFP net-event/drop audit has been enabled or claimed.

## Recovery

1. Send a current nonce/sequence `unblock`, then check matching `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, active false, engine false, empty filters, and the real NAT recovery control.
2. Send current `exit`, or press Ctrl+C in the manually opened helper console. Both close the dynamic session and terminate.
3. If the controller/HDC is unavailable, use the helper console's Ctrl+C. As a last local recovery, the user may terminate only the recorded helper PID after checking its executable path/StartTime. Terminating this management process ends the dynamic WFP session; do not kill unrelated Emulator or HDC processes.
4. Unexpected process death also ends the dynamic session by the official WFP lifecycle contract. A stale status file is not a live acknowledgment; independently confirm restored same-endpoint HEAD/GET. There are no persistent/boot-time rules to restore, no global defaults were changed, and no broad cleanup rule should be run.

The independent sequence remains online positive control → scoped block plus same-endpoint failure/zero arrivals and host-service liveness → three cancellation cases with full evidence → unblock/exit and same-endpoint recovery. Check HDC heartbeat and lawful reconnection throughout. A guest may still report eth0/NetConn available: this helper targets transmission isolation, not the guest network-manager state. Do not report R27 passed until the root agent reviews the independent evidence and this boundary.

## Primary references

Native types/constants/GUIDs are based on Microsoft's [WinSDK fwpmtypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwpmtypes.h), [fwptypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwptypes.h), [fwpmu.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/fwpmu.h) and [rpcdce.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/rpcdce.h). Relevant APIs: [EngineOpen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmengineopen0), [FilterAdd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0), [FilterGetById](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfiltergetbyid0), [SubLayerAdd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmsublayeradd0), [Object Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/object-management). L37:       [in]  HANDLE         engineHandle,
